bill.title: Wabeno Economic Development Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 494.
bill.officialSummary: Wabeno Economic Development Act This bill requires the Forest Service to convey approximately 14 acres of federal land, including the mineral rights, in the Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest, Wisconsin, to Tony's Wabeno Redi-Mix, LLC, upon receiving an offer to buy the land for market value. The Forest Service must complete an appraisal to determine the market value of the land, and the offer must be received within 180 days after federal approval of such appraisal. Tony's Wabeno Redi-Mix, LLC, must pay an amount equal to the market value of the land and all associated costs as a condition of conveyance. Additionally, the Department of the Interior must publish a comprehensive review of the federal permitting processes for the development of stone, sand, and gravel on federal lands.

classification.plainSummary: This bill directs the Forest Service to sell approximately 14 acres of federal land in Wisconsin's Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest to a specific company, Tony's Wabeno Redi-Mix, LLC, at market value if the company makes an offer within 180 days of an appraisal. The company must pay the appraised value plus all transaction costs. The bill also requires the Department of the Interior to publish a review of federal permitting processes for developing stone, sand, and gravel on federal lands.

industries.rationale: The bill facilitates a land transfer to a ready-mix concrete company and mandates a review of permitting for sand, gravel, and stone extraction on federal lands.
Ready-mix concrete operations supply the construction sector, and changes to aggregate permitting processes could affect construction material costs and availability.

plain.whatItDoes: This bill would require the Forest Service to convey approximately 14 acres of federal land. That includes the mineral rights, in the Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest, Wisconsin, to Tony's Wabeno Redi-Mix, LLC, upon receiving an offer to buy the land for market value.

plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in what may be done on that land. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
